summary.title: Summary
paragraphs: Senior engineer with {{OVERALL_EXPERIENCE_YEARS}} years in JavaScript and TypeScript, frontend-heavy full stack. Since 2022, building the real-time trading frontend of XBO.com, a crypto exchange: heavy WebSocket traffic where performance matters, exact decimal money math, 17 languages. Before that, frontend tech lead at robota.ua, the largest job board in Ukraine.

As independent projects, built the whole technical side of ELI, an AI English tutor with 52 active paid subscriptions (Whisper and LLM voice pipeline, serverless AWS, Stripe billing), designed and built Mrrlin, a workspace for coding agents, and built alone the agent harness that runs both products' operations.

entries.name: Senior Frontend Engineer · XBO.com, crypto exchange
entries.descr: Web trading frontend and client area of a crypto exchange: spot, futures and CFDs.
bullets: Designed the real-time data layer on SignalR/WebSockets: order books, charts, tickers and positions update in under a second.
Kept the UI responsive under high-frequency streams with RxJS-based state management.
Moved trading calculations to arbitrary-precision arithmetic and built type-safe order forms with real-time validation.
Ships client-area flows with the backend, QA and compliance teams (withdrawals, fiat bank-account whitelisting, DAC8 reporting data) in 17 languages.

Since mid-2026, delivers through an agent workflow of his own around the team's Azure DevOps flow: agents turn user stories into implementation-ready specs, coding agents implement in isolated git worktrees, a multi-model consensus gate reviews the design and each of his PRs, and browser and Figma QA agents verify the result.

entries.name: Frontend Engineer → Frontend Tech Lead · robota.ua
entries.descr: The largest job board in Ukraine (6.5M+ resumes). Grew from mid-level engineer to tech lead of the frontend platform.
bullets: Moved the 20-year-old product's .NET/jQuery monolith to Angular + GraphQL services; built the mobile SPA from scratch.
Cut CI builds from about 40 to about 20 minutes (TeamCity to GitHub Actions, incremental builds, caching).
Moved key pages from red to green Core Web Vitals; introduced TypeScript strict mode, SonarQube and Sentry.

entries.name: ELI, AI English tutor · built the whole technical side
entries.descr: Co-founded with partners who run the business side. Pronunciation and goal-based speaking practice (job interviews, work meetings, relocation). Live, as of 11/2026: 52 active paid subscriptions, ~780 registered users.
bullets: Built the voice pipeline: Whisper speech recognition on serverless GPU and phoneme-level pronunciation scoring.
Fine-tuned GPT models for the tutor's dialogue (LangChain), driven by a learner profile updated after every conversation.
Built the serverless, event-driven AWS backend (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, DynamoDB, CloudFront, Cognito) plus GCP/Firebase, and Stripe subscriptions tiered by speaking minutes.

entries.name: Mrrlin, workspace for coding agents · designed and built
entries.descr: Co-founded, in beta; its founders use it to build ELI and Mrrlin. A Director turns one goal into a task plan and routes tasks to Claude Code, Codex CLI and other models. Separately, built alone the agent harness that runs the day-to-day operations of both products in production.
bullets: Mrrlin: a TypeScript monorepo with a Next.js 15 operator dashboard, a Hono REST API with shared Zod schemas and generated OpenAPI, Supabase PostgreSQL with Row Level Security, and Stripe subscriptions; tested with pgTAP, Playwright end-to-end tests and a fast CI gate.
Task state lives in a strictly typed PostgreSQL state machine with atomic transition checks and sticky agent assignment, replacing flat Markdown task files.

Its public npm package @mrrlin-dev/mcp (about 27,000 downloads in 30 days, Nov 2026), an MCP server plus a background bridge that runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, lets a local Claude Code or Codex agent take Mrrlin tasks and run each one in its own git worktree, leaving the operator's working copy untouched; weak output goes back through multi-model consensus review, and a task closes only with proof (a live URL, a green build or a human sign-off).

The harness: an always-on Hermes Agent plus a TypeScript service (Node.js, Hono, SQLite) with leases for parallel agents and idempotency keys, steered from Telegram, one channel per workflow. It runs SEO end to end, directs and produces TikTok videos in Google Flow, handles the helpdesk (refunds and support), posts to social networks, reacts to alerts and ships quick product changes straight from Telegram.
Review gates: independent reviewer models score outgoing messages against hard rules before they go out.
